messages:
alex: quick heads-up ":wave:" opened a PR to update the Dedicated provisioning migration guide. key fixes: clarify SLA wording for eviction windows, add a small SDK snippet for the new scale_policy shape, and repair two broken internal anchor links. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1503

maya: can you paste the SDK snippet here so I can sanity-check the fields against the client?

alex: sure, dropping a minimal example we intend to include:
```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient()
policy = {
  "mode": "autoscale",
  "cooldown_seconds": 60,
  "queue_limit": 300,
  "burst_capacity": 1,
  "fallback_policy": "reserved-pool-fallback"
}
client.set_scale_policy(tenant_id="acct-42", policy=policy)
```

tom: looks good. small rename request: in code we use `cooldown_sec` in the SDK right now. either update the docs to match or push an SDK alias. prefer alias to avoid churn.

nina: editorial: SLA line currently says "eviction may occur within X minutes" which sounded like a guarantee. suggest: "In capacity-constrained scenarios, lower-priority tenants may be evicted after the configured fallback window."

alex: accepted. will replace with your wording and add a one-line example timeline: "scale-up attempt: immediate -> warmstart 1-3s -> if still insufficient after 2m, fallback policies may apply."

maya: linkfix note: the anchor broken is from the legacy section header `#eviction-examples`. changed heading id to `#eviction-behavior-examples` in my branch; please update cross-links.

docs-ci: lint: ok, linkcheck: 2 anchors fixed, 0 remaining.

alex: thanks all. nina, can you add the short translator comment for the SLA sentence? just one line like: // context: explains that eviction is an outcome of fallback policy, not a guaranteed action.

nina: done in the PR body.

alex: plan: i'll squash the minor edits, leave the SDK alias discussion to tom/maya offline, and merge once CI shows green. target: end of week. :rocket:
